title: MCP access to balances
outcome: An MCP client (e.g. Claude) can call a get_balances tool on this app's deployed MCP route and receive the same grouped-by-institution balance data the dashboard page shows, authenticated by a static bearer API key. Deployment infrastructure itself (Vercel project, GitHub connection, Deployment Protection, real secrets) is already set up by the maintainer outside this milestone -- this milestone is code only.

included: Refactor the SimpleFin fetch logic m1 built inside the dashboard's Server Component into a shared server-only module, reused by both the dashboard page and the new MCP route -- no behavior change to the existing page.
An MCP route (e.g. app/mcp/route.ts) exposing exactly one tool, get_balances, returning the same grouped-by-institution balance data as the dashboard page.

App-level static bearer-token authentication on the MCP route: a single API key read from a server-side-only env var (e.g. MCP_BEARER_KEY), compared with crypto.timingSafeEqual, checked via an Authorization: Bearer header or a ?key= query param (matching js/ember-finance's pattern, which specifically avoids returning a bare 401 that triggers an MCP client's OAuth auto-registration attempt).
A .env.example entry documenting MCP_BEARER_KEY as a required secret, with a comment that it must never be committed.
Tests: the MCP route rejects a missing/wrong bearer key, accepts the correct one, and its responses (success and error) never contain the SimpleFin access URL or its embedded credential.
Tests and any manual verification run against SimpleFin's public demo bridge, never a real linked account -- same principle as m1.
excluded: Any actual deployment action (Vercel project creation, GitHub App authorization, Deployment Protection toggling, Protection Bypass secret generation, setting real env vars in Vercel) -- these are already done or remain maintainer actions outside any task.

Real OAuth 2.1 (the MCP spec's mandated pattern, as implemented by js/ember via Supabase) -- explicitly deferred; this app has no user-account system to delegate to. Noted as a spec-compliance tradeoff in docs/product/PURPOSE.md, not silently ignored.
Any additional MCP tools beyond get_balances (no per-account queries, no transaction history).
Pushing commits anywhere -- same as m1, the orchestrator commits to the local dev branch only.
Editing pnpm-workspace.yaml, .orchestrator/policy.json, or any file outside this repository's own directory.

behaviors.description: A request to the MCP route with a correct bearer key successfully invokes get_balances and returns the same grouped-by-institution balance data as the dashboard page, using SimpleFin's public demo bridge.

A request to the MCP route with a missing or incorrect bearer key is rejected, without ever attempting the SimpleFin call and without returning a bare 401 that would trigger an MCP client's OAuth auto-registration flow (matching js/ember-finance's documented reasoning).

Neither a successful nor an error response from the MCP route ever contains the SimpleFin access URL, its embedded credential, or SimpleFin's raw auth headers -- verified by an automated test, not just code review.
The existing m1 dashboard page continues to render correctly after the SimpleFin-fetch refactor -- same behavior, now backed by the shared module instead of inline fetch logic.
